Q1: Which conflicted paths should get the fail-closed check (resolved lines must come from one of the two merge sides, in order, with no extra duplicates)?
Choices:
A. Today's `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/`, plus the existing protected-path list the deterministic review skip already uses (`PROTECTED_SKIP_SUPPRESSED`): `.github/`, `.claude/`, `scripts/`, `prompts/`, `workflow-templates/`, `validation/`, `ai-memory/`, `db/contracts/`, agent-instruction files at any depth (`agents.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `unattended_system_instructions.md`), and root build/dependency/lint config. These would be defined once in the verifier and covered by a contract test. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Only `.github/` (all of it) and `scripts/`. This closes the reported attack path with the fewest new rejections, but leaves `prompts/`, `.claude/` hooks, `workflow-templates/` and root config unchecked.
C. Every conflicted path, with no allowlist. This is the strongest guarantee, but the judge could then never write a merged line for any conflict, including application code in consumer repos. Integration conflicts that need one would keep failing to publish until the integration-sync lifetime cap stops the project.
